description: FTT_StandAlone contains a family of evolutionary technology-transition models for power, heat, transport, freight and other energy uses. Coupled Lotka-Volterra equations represent competing technology shares. The provider is cpmodel (repository owner). Coverage: The software is generic, not a measured geographic dataset. Spatial detail and simulation periods are supplied by the user. Access: The public source repository provides documentation and installation instructions. Source archives and dependencies were not downloaded or run. Licence and cost: The repository identifies MIT for this Python implementation. Input data and coupled macroeconomic tools have separate terms. Limitations: Input vintages differ: the README lists heat data through 2020 and some power, freight and transport inputs through 2022 or 2023. The hydrogen module is marked under review. For simulation it supports energy-policy and technology-transition scenarios. Related resources: This is the standalone Python family, distinct from the FORTRAN version coupled to E3ME.
